# Wire proxy/prompts/author.txt into the author model system_prompt config

## Problem statement

The `author` model alias in `proxy/config.yaml` has no `system_prompt` block, so the wiki authoring guidelines in `proxy/prompts/author.txt` (116 lines, including the "explain names on first mention" rule from LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) are never loaded by the proxy. No client supplies the content client-side, so the prompt currently has zero effect — the completed LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE deliverable is unreachable through the proxy's auto-loading path.

## Users

- **Wiki authoring operators** invoking the `author` alias (directly or via an authoring client) — they expect the mandatory wiki guidelines to shape every `author` response.
- **Readers of the open_source_llm wiki** — indirectly benefit from consistent openness terminology, citation, and naming conventions.

Example user stories:

- As an operator authoring wiki content via the `author` alias, I want the proxy to inject `proxy/prompts/author.txt` into my requests so that terminology/openness classification and citation rules are applied without me having to paste the guidelines each time.
- As a wiki reader, I want model categories consistently labelled (open-source vs open-weights vs closed) and project/concept names explained at first mention (LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) so pages are accurate and navigable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config.yaml` gains a `system_prompt` block on the `author` entry with `mode: "override"` and `file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"`, and config validation passes at load time.
- [ ] A test asserts `resolve_system_prompt("author", model_cfg)` against the real config returns the author.txt content (mode `override`, correct `source` path); an injection-path test asserts an `author` request's system messages are replaced by author.txt content (mode `override`).
- [ ] The proxy auto-loading path is verified live: a `model=author` request through `proxy_openai_api` applies the resolved prompt (first real-world use of the `system_prompt` feature).
- [ ] Documentation is updated to reflect the wiring, including `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (author as a worked `system_prompt` example) and code comments as needed.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (build → test → commit order).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Keep the `system_prompt` schema as documented in `proxy/config.yaml` (lines 113–127): optional block, `mode` ∈ {override, prepend} (required), `file` relative to repo root.
- Resolution precedence must be preserved: local override (`.sorraAgents/prompts/author.txt`, currently absent) → repo default (`proxy/prompts/author.txt`).
- `author.txt` must stay within the resolver's max file size (64 KB); content changes are out of scope here (author.txt content is owned by LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE / prompt-content work).
- No changes to the resolver or request-handling code unless a defect is found while wiring; prefer configuration-only change.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml` author entry (lines 334–408) has providers only; no `system_prompt` block.
- `resolve_system_prompt()` (`proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py:82`) returns `None` when `model_cfg["system_prompt"]` is absent.
- `proxy_openai_api` (`proxy/proxy/ui.py:1254`) is the live injection point for `/v1/chat/completions`; `compose_messages` applies override/prepend.
- No model entry in `config.yaml` currently has an active `system_prompt` block — author becomes the first live use.
- No client in `~/projects`, `~/.pi`, or the open_source_llm tooling references author.txt or its content; only `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py:436` reads it.

## Desired change

1. Add the `system_prompt` block to the `author` entry in `proxy/config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   author:
     providers:
       # ... existing providers unchanged ...
     system_prompt:
       mode: "override"   # operator-confirmed; replaces client system messages
       file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"
   ```

2. Add tests: real-config resolution for `author` → author.txt (mode `override`), plus an injection-path assertion that an `author` request's system messages are replaced.
3. Document the wiring in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (worked example) and any code comments.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Add `system_prompt` block to the `author` entry (lines 334–408).
- `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py` — Reference only; no change expected (resolution + precedence already implemented).
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — Reference only; `proxy_openai_api` already applies resolved prompts (no change expected).
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py` — Add test asserting `resolve_system_prompt("author", model_cfg)` returns author.txt with mode `override`.
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_injection_integration.py` — Add/extend test asserting `author` requests get system messages replaced (mode `override`).
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — Document author as the worked `system_prompt` example.
- `proxy/README.md` — Update if it lists per-model features.

## Related work

- `Add 'explain project and concept names at first use' rule to the author system prompt (LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE)` — completed; discoverer. Its deliverable lives in author.txt but is currently unreachable; this task makes it effective.
- `Assign custom system prompts to model aliases (LP-0MNXBI97B00773WF)` — completed; introduced the `system_prompt` config feature.
- `Config schema & validation (LP-0MPXTZ71W0024ISW)` — completed; schema + validation for `system_prompt`.
- `Prompt resolver (LP-0MPXTZAG0001BMHU)` — completed; implemented `resolve_system_prompt`.
- `Prompt resolution tests (LP-0MPXTYWL70047KKD)` — completed; base test coverage for resolution.
- `Config: plan and code aliases (LP-0MQ5BMWO1001HRLV)` — completed; noted `system_prompt` blocks could be added per alias later (this task does exactly that for author).
- `Add author fallback model with same fallback chain as plan (LP-0MRPDJ2XF005Y9XN)` — completed; predecessor author wiring.
- `Binding registry and restricted-model detection (LP-0MSMFQ8SU003PJV9)` — completed; surfaced by find-related, moderate relevance (alias↔model binding machinery adjacent to config wiring).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — override is destructive:** `mode: "override"` replaces *all* system messages for `author` requests, including any client-supplied system prompt. Assumption (operator-confirmed): the author client sends no needed client-side system prompt, and author.txt is intended as the complete system prompt for authoring. Mitigation: document this in MODEL_ADD.md and note the local-override escape hatch (`.sorraAgents/prompts/author.txt`) for per-deployment overrides.
- **Assumption:** no client currently injects author.txt content client-side — verified by repo-wide search; if a client later sends its own copy, precedence/duplication should be revisited.
- **Assumption:** no resolver/handler code changes are needed; if wiring reveals a defect, scope a follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Scope-creep guard:** author.txt *content* changes (rules, wording) are already owned by LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE and out of scope here; this task is wiring + tests + docs only.

## Open questions (resolved)

- **Original open question** (from description): does the wiki authoring client already send author.txt as a client-supplied system message? — **Resolved:** no client reference found anywhere; proxy auto-load is the correct path (operator confirm + repo search).
- **Mode override vs prepend** — **Resolved by operator: `override`.**

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSMFQ8SU003PJV9** – Binding registry and restricted-model detection (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ06M5007CPN6** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:10 — Expected a statement (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ072M0085AF5** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:12 — Expected `,`, found name (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — keyword match (prompt-text dataset; low relevance)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — keyword match (prompt-text dataset; low relevance)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — keyword match (prompt-text dataset; low relevance)

> Note: the two LP-0MSXZ… logrotate items and the ds4 rendered-prompt files are keyword-matching noise, not substantive related work.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which injection mode should the author `system_prompt` block use?" — Answer (operator): **B) `override`** — replaces all system messages with author.txt. Recommended was A) prepend (advisory); operator's choice proceeded. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the proxy auto-load author.txt, or does the wiki authoring client already supply this content client-side?" — Answer (operator): **A) Proxy auto-loads it**. Recommended was A. Research: searched `~/projects`, `~/.pi`, open_source_llm tooling — zero references to author.txt or its content outside `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py:436`; `resolve_system_prompt` returns `None` for author (no config block). Source: interactive reply + repo search.

data.description:
**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** task (verification) · **Priority:** high

## Problem

The proxy already emits the composed "All providers exhausted" retry contract
(`Retry-After` header + matching `retry_after` body field, stable `code`, no
over-long chain-hold), but the existing end-to-end test
(`proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`, from LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG) does
**not** pin the composed contract tightly enough to catch every regression:

- it asserts `retry_after > 0` and that the header matches the body, but never
  asserts the value **equals** the real soonest availability computed under a
  pinned clock (AC2);
- it exercises the generic `code: all_exhausted` path end-to-end, but the
  sole-cause time-window `code: outside_time_window` variant is asserted only
  against the response builder (`test_exhaustion_error_code.py`), not through
  the fallback chain with the retry timer (AC3);
- the client-recognition prose (`error == "All providers exhausted"`) and the
  bounded-hold guarantee are asserted, but not as one pinned regression for
  the retry timer (AC1, AC4, AC5).

## Change

Harden the end-to-end exhaustion test so the whole "no models available" retry
contract is pinned and fails if any part regresses. Extend the existing test
file — do **not** duplicate the window+quarantine or lease-denied scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Retry timer present and consistent:** A deterministic end-to-end test
  drives the in-process proxy with every provider unavailable and asserts the
  terminal `503` "All providers exhausted" response carries **both** a
  `Retry-After` HTTP header (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body
  field, with the **same value**.
- **AC2 — Timeless truthfulness:** The asserted `retry_after` equals the real
  soonest availability (the maximum of cooldown durations, `available_times`
  window edges, and usage-limit reset times), is positive whenever a provider is
  genuinely blocked, and is `0` only when availability exists. The test pins the
  clock/value so the assertion is deterministic.
- **AC3 — Both exhaustion variants covered:** The verification covers the generic
  `code: "all_exhausted"` path and the time-window `code: "outside_time_window"`
  path (both are "All providers exhausted" 503s), asserting the same retry-timer
  contract on each.
- **AC4 — Client-recognition contract intact:** The response retains
  `error == "All providers exhausted"` and a stable `code`, and the existing
  exhaustion-contract tests still pass (additive-only; no prose/code change).
- **AC5 — No hold longer than the timer:** When a chain-hold would exceed the
  retry timer, the exhaustion response is surfaced immediately with the timer
  rather than held beyond it (bounded by `retry_after`). Verified in the same or
  a paired test.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`: reuse `_FixedDateTime`, `_DummyRequest`, the provider-state reset fixture and the `_record_hold` monkeypatch already in the file.
- Add a sole-cause window case with all providers outside `available_times` and no cooldown/quarantine, asserting `code == "outside_time_window"` plus the matching `Retry-After`/`retry_after`.
- For the window+quarantine case, pin the expected value (window edge in seconds under `_FixedDateTime`) and assert `retry_after == <expected>` exactly, that `_compute_retry_after` under the same clock equals it, and that the header equals the body string.
- Assert the `0` edge case (`_build_exhausted_response()` with no blockers → `retry_after == 0`).
- Keep determinism: monkeypatch `_hold_sleep` to record; assert no real sleep.
- No code change to `proxy/proxy/provider.py` is expected; if a genuine gap is found, raise a bug work item and record the blocking relationship instead of widening scope.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py` — the extended E2E retry-timer assertions (primary).
- `proxy/tests/test_honest_retry_after.py` — reuse its pinned-clock expectations for the window-edge arithmetic.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_retry_after_bound.py` — reference for the bounded-hold assertions.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference: `_compute_retry_after` (~2383), `_build_exhausted_response` (~3177), `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (~3241).

## Deliverables

- Test diff with the pinned retry-timer assertions for both exhaustion variants and the bounded-hold guarantee.
- Recorded test-run output (targeted file + full suite) as evidence on this work item.
data.title: E2E retry-timer contract verification (all-exhausted + time-window)
